convert-tohexstring.title: Format bytes as hexadecimal with Convert.ToHexString
convert-tohexstring.short: Convert binary data to hex without a manual loop
convert-tohexstring.summary: Convert.ToHexString converts a byte sequence directly to an uppercase hexadecimal string.
convert-tohexstring.why: It avoids custom format loops and clearly communicates that the output is a hexadecimal representation of bytes.
convert-tohexstring.tips: Use Convert.FromHexString for the reverse operation and validate external input when decoding.

rune-unicode-scalar.title: Process Unicode scalar values with Rune
rune-unicode-scalar.short: Do not assume one char equals one visible code point
rune-unicode-scalar.summary: Rune represents a Unicode scalar value and EnumerateRunes walks a string without splitting supplementary characters into separate UTF-16 code units.
rune-unicode-scalar.why: char is a UTF-16 code unit, so character-oriented algorithms can break text outside the Basic Multilingual Plane when they iterate char by char.
rune-unicode-scalar.tips: Grapheme clusters can still contain multiple Rune values; use text-element APIs when the unit you need is a user-perceived character.

iparsable-generic-parsing.title: Write generic parsers with IParsable<T>
iparsable-generic-parsing.short: Express parsing support as a generic constraint
iparsable-generic-parsing.summary: IParsable<T> exposes static Parse and TryParse members so generic code can parse types that implement a common contract.
iparsable-generic-parsing.why: It removes type switches and per-type parsing delegates from reusable parsing helpers.
iparsable-generic-parsing.tips: Use ISpanParsable<T> when parsing directly from spans matters for allocation-sensitive code.

http-completion-responseheadersread.title: Stream HTTP bodies with ResponseHeadersRead
http-completion-responseheadersread.short: Return after headers instead of buffering the full body
http-completion-responseheadersread.summary: HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead makes GetAsync complete after response headers are available, allowing the body stream to be consumed progressively.
http-completion-responseheadersread.why: Large downloads can start processing sooner and avoid unnecessary whole-response buffering.
http-completion-responseheadersread.tips: Keep the HttpResponseMessage alive while consuming its content stream and pass cancellation through the read operations.

json-deserialize-async-enumerable.title: Stream JSON arrays with DeserializeAsyncEnumerable
json-deserialize-async-enumerable.summary: JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsyncEnumerable<T> exposes elements from a JSON array as an IAsyncEnumerable<T> while reading from a stream.
json-deserialize-async-enumerable.why: It can reduce peak memory and let processing begin before a large JSON array has been fully materialized.
json-deserialize-async-enumerable.tips: Enumeration owns the ongoing read; propagate cancellation and finish or dispose the surrounding stream according to its ownership contract.

regex-match-timeout.title: Set a timeout for potentially expensive regular expressions
regex-match-timeout.short: Bound regex matching time for untrusted input
regex-match-timeout.summary: Regex constructors can take a match timeout that limits how long a matching operation may run before RegexMatchTimeoutException is thrown.
regex-match-timeout.why: Certain patterns and inputs can require unexpectedly large amounts of backtracking, so a timeout provides a defensive upper bound.
regex-match-timeout.tips: A timeout is not a substitute for reviewing the pattern; also catch RegexMatchTimeoutException at an appropriate boundary.

operating-system-platform-check.title: Check the current platform with OperatingSystem helpers
operating-system-platform-check.summary: OperatingSystem.IsWindows, IsLinux, IsMacOS and related helpers express runtime platform checks directly.
operating-system-platform-check.why: They are clearer than manually interpreting platform identifiers and are understood by platform compatibility analysis.
operating-system-platform-check.tips: Keep platform-specific code behind a small boundary so most application logic remains portable.

ziparchive-create-entry.title: Create ZIP entries with ZipArchive
ziparchive-create-entry.short: Write files into a ZIP archive as streams
ziparchive-create-entry.summary: ZipArchive.CreateEntry creates an entry whose Open method returns a stream for writing that entry's contents.
ziparchive-create-entry.why: It supports archive creation without first building each entry as a separate in-memory byte array.
ziparchive-create-entry.tips: Disposing the archive finalizes archive metadata; use leaveOpen when the caller must continue using the underlying stream.

file-move-overwrite.title: Replace a destination while moving with File.Move
file-move-overwrite.short: Use the overwrite overload when replacement is intended
file-move-overwrite.summary: File.Move(source, destination, overwrite: true) moves a file and permits an existing destination file to be replaced.
file-move-overwrite.why: It expresses replacement intent directly instead of a separate existence check followed by delete and move operations.
file-move-overwrite.tips: Filesystem operations can still fail because of permissions, locks, invalid paths, or cross-filesystem behavior; handle the errors your application can recover from.

enumerable-minby.title: Select the element with the smallest key using MinBy
enumerable-minby.short: Get the source element associated with a minimum
enumerable-minby.summary: MinBy returns the source element whose selected key is smallest, such as the least-loaded server.
enumerable-minby.why: It avoids computing Min and then enumerating again to locate an element with that key.
enumerable-minby.tips: Define the empty-sequence behavior your code expects and provide a comparer when the default key ordering is not appropriate.
